title: Wafer Geometry Measurement - Crystal Originated Particles (COP) Detection on ATL/LMS IPRO8
subtitle: Pre-Bonding Quality Validation for 7nm Node Manufacturing
author: Dr. Priya Sharma

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the ATL/LMS IPRO8 system to detect and classify Crystal Originated Particles (COP) defects during pre-bonding inspection at the 7nm technology node. The test is conducted at Singapore Fab 7 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 300mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Crystal Originated Particles (COP) defects that are critical to yield at the 7nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the ATL/LMS IPRO8 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: ATL/LMS IPRO8
- Inspection Type: Wafer Geometry Measurement
- Target Defect: Crystal Originated Particles (COP)
- Process Step: Pre-Bonding
- Wafer Size: 300mm
- Technology Node: 7nm
- Fab Location: Singapore Fab 7

This test case applies to all ATL/LMS IPRO8 systems deployed at Singapore Fab 7 for pre-bonding monitoring in the 7nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: ATL/LMS IPRO8
Software Version: v15.1.394
Recipe: WAFER_GEOMETRY_MEASUREMENT_7nm_PRE_BONDING
Illumination Mode: Darkfield
Scan Speed: Low (146 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 1.0μm
Edge Exclusion: 2mm
Sampling Plan: 5-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the ATL/LMS IPRO8 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Wafer Geometry Measurement' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Crystal Originated Particles (COP) defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 7nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 107 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 92% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±1.0% for Wafer Geometry Measurement
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.96 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2025-01-31
Wafers Tested: 49
Total Defects Found: 1569
Defect Density: 221.97 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 2.0%
Capture Rate: 89.4%
Test Duration: 247 minutes
System Uptime: 98.6%

Result Classification: CONDITIONAL PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The ATL/LMS IPRO8 demonstrated acceptable performance in detecting Crystal Originated Particles (COP) at the 7nm node.

b) The capture rate requires optimization of the detection algorithm.

c) Nuisance rate is within acceptable limits.

d) Edge-zone defect detection showed improved performance compared to previous revision.

e) SECS/GEM communication was verified with zero packet loss during data transfer.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Review edge-zone detection parameters for optimization.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Monitor performance over next 30 production days.
